desc: Implement a helper function `count_with_cost(n, k)` that returns the number of integers in $[1, n]$ that have cost $k$ (i.e., require $k$ divisions by 4 to become 0). This is done by intersecting $[1, n]$ with $[4^{k-1}, 4^k - 1]$.
For each query $[l, r]$, determine the maximum cost $M$ which is the cost of $r$.

Iterate over all possible cost values $k$ (from 1 to 30, since $4^{30} > 10^{18} > 10^9$) to calculate the total sum of costs $S$ for the range $[l, r]$ by summing $k \times (\text{count\_with\_cost}(r, k) - \text{count\_with\_cost}(l-1, k))$.
Compute the result for the query as $\max(M, (S + 1) // 2)$ and add it to the total sum.
Return the total sum of results for all queries.
